note: The browser rows are measured on the nightly runner (ubuntu-24.04-arm, headless Chromium, seed 7, 60 s a row), from the audio-quality-run artifacts of seven scheduled Nightly runs on main each. The AAC rows come from the seven after the estimator began measuring a reordered frame against the frames before it, 2026-10-14 to 2026-10-20 (38564590314, 38733214352, 38897397428, 39027965381, 39124936449, 39266265648, 39421743227); the Opus rows come from the seven before it, 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-13 (37633358782, 37790146216, 37940662573, 38054566400, 38143901976, 38276133321, 38415278161). Each ceiling is the worst of its seven nights times 1.25, plus one runner hiccup, rounded up to two significant figures. The hiccup is sized from the single gaps the 2026-10-08 night put on otherwise clean rows, the fixed-250 control among them: 250 underruns/min, 700 gap ms/min, 3.3 skips/min, 280 discarded ms/min, 0.01 stalled, 0.015 silence, and one 20 ms bucket of target. Budgeted this way, every night passes when it is held out of its row's measurement except one, and that row's own ceiling includes it: 0.75 s of main-thread long tasks on the 2026-10-17 AAC step row, which stalled it and lifted its target to 803 ms. These ceilings record today's player as the runner hears it, not target audio quality. The AAC bursty rows stall for at most 0.041 of the window, against 0.018 for Opus bursty on the same nights, but still discard up to 870 ms a minute against its 210. To re-measure, download the same artifact from the latest scheduled nightlies (`gh run download <id> -n audio-quality-run`), which keep every run, and apply the same rule. The replay rows are deterministic, so their ceilings are exactly what they measured, through the end of each recording, with no headroom: any regression fails them, and an improvement should be tightened in. They were last re-measured on 2026-10-22 using version 3 traces with encoded frame durations: AAC-LC uses its fixed 1024 samples, and relay-mic was re-recorded with Chromium's fake device, retaining Opus packet TOC durations (35 s, minimum RTT 2 ms). This is not real-microphone or added-RTT validation. The local-aac replay's stalled ceiling rises from 0.008 to 0.017 and silence from 0.015 to 0.020 because replay no longer stretches each frame to nearby timestamp gaps; the production player is unchanged. All other changed replay ceilings tighten to the exact measurement. Browser and native ceilings are unchanged. bursty-aac is the 2026-10-18 AAC bursty isolated capture, recorded with the observer subscribed at the decoder's 2 s budget, so it holds every group the player saw. The native rows are provisional: measured on a loaded developer host (x86_64 Linux, the private PulseAudio null sink, seed 7, 60 s a row) on 2026-10-17, three runs of every row from the debug build nightly uses plus three more of the AAC rows from a release build, which played alike. Each ceiling is the worst clean run times 1.25, plus one native hiccup sized from the unimpaired Opus row's worst run (20 underruns/min, 50 gap ms/min, 2.2 skips/min, 110 discarded ms/min, 0.01 stalled, 0.005 silence, one 20 ms bucket of target), rounded up to two significant figures. On that host the null sink's clock ran about 150 ppm slow against the monotonic clock, read within 5 ms at p95 per sample, and its output latency sat between 14 and 28 ms. Five of the 36 AAC rows (none of the 18 Opus rows) voided on the clock: the device stopped pulling for about two seconds mid-row, sometimes after a backend error and a stream restart, which is a native playback defect rather than noise, and the ceilings exclude those runs. Re-measure from the nightly runner's artifacts once it has a week of native rows.
